source.title: Refusal Is Not Robustness: Measuring Harmful Reachability in Autoregressive Language Models
source.authors: Parv Kapoor; Teresa Fortes; Cláudia Mamede; Rui Abreu; Jonathan Aldrich; Eunsuk Kang

page_placements.theme: Opening-token and sparse decoding interventions change safety

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Conceptually tests whether jailbreak transformations can elicit harmful responses, using an 18-template attack library and empirical ASR rather than fine-tuning or measuring response-position KL.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that the 18-template library includes compliant-prefix and suffix forcing, but gives only aggregate empirical ASR across the library, not results for those templates individually. It does not test fine-tuning, response-position KL, literal response prefilling, decoding changes, safety localization in weights, or methods to deepen safety. BCA reachability and adaptive-search results are not recorded as rows because they do not isolate the compliant-prefix/suffix effect or report its specific completion rate.
record.test_reason: The study uses jailbreak attacks (an 18-template library, PAIR and TAP) as tools for evaluating its own BCA/GAS diagnostic. Its only ASR numbers are aggregates over a library dominated by persona, narrative, format and permission framings. Compliant-prefix and suffix-forcing templates are never broken out, and there is no literal response prefilling, decoding-change result or per-position analysis. So no result isolates whether getting past the opening tokens defeats refusal (V4). Shallow alignment (Qi et al.) appears only in related work. BCA's hidden harmful mass under greedy refusal is a probability score over a bounded top-k tree, a related but different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that ASR on sampled outputs hides harmful probability mass in alternative continuations. They argue BCA separates models with identical greedy ASR, correlates with independently sampled harmful generations, and complements judge-guided search in red teaming.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates jailbreak transformations and harmful continuation reachability; it does not fine-tune models or measure aligned-versus-base KL by response position.
record.method_sensitivity: The aggregate empirical ASR differs by target model under the 18-template attack library.

fits_no_version.finding: All four models have 0% greedy ASR on direct JailbreakBench prompts. Yet bounded harmful continuation mass (GAS@0; α=0.99, k=2, L=8) ranges from 0.002 (Llama-3.1-8B) to 0.211 (Mistral-7B).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Greedy refusal can coexist with non-trivial harmful probability mass in nearby high-probability alternative continuations, varying widely across models.

fits_no_version.finding: Under an aggregate 18-template jailbreak library, empirical ASR is 100% for Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen2.5-7B and Mistral-7B, and 76.7% for Llama-3.1-8B. Template-level BCA mass correlates with sampled ASR (Spearman 0.53–0.73).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mixed prompt-level jailbreak libraries elicit harmful completions from greedily-refusing instruct models; this does not isolate an opening-token mechanism.

record.problems: The reported attack-library ASR aggregates across 18 transformations, so it does not show which transformation produced the harmful completions. The paper states that reachability results depend on the specific judge checkpoints and that probabilistic target models introduce variance; no uncertainty estimates are given for Table 1.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were included: the paper does not report separate ASR values for compliant-prefix or suffix-forcing templates, nor results for literal response prefilling or decoding changes.

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models; no position-wise analysis.
No isolated prefilling, compliant-prefix, suffix or decoding-change results; compliant-prefix/suffix templates are only pooled in an 18-template library.
No analysis of the data or objective causing shallowness.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 link rests on the library merely including compliant-prefix and suffix-forcing templates, which the paper never reports separately. The authors claim BCA 'operationalizes' shallow alignment, but they report no first-token or prefill evidence. TAP/PAIR results (Tables 3–4) concern the BCA search signal, not any claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning and its effect on refusal.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.

The paper reports only aggregate outcomes for a library that includes compliant-prefix and suffix-forcing transformations; it does not isolate their effects. Literal response prefilling and decoding changes are not tested.
Whether safety behavior is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether data or training objectives cause shallow safety.
Training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens and its robustness.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Applied a fixed library of 18 jailbreak transformations, including compliant-prefix and suffix-forcing strategies; reported aggregate empirical ASR.
rows.measure: Empirical ASR@18: fraction of behaviors where any template elicited a judged-harmful completion
rows.note: Aggregate over the library; the result does not identify the contribution of compliant-prefix or suffix-forcing templates separately.
rows.check: Empirical ASR@18 (100%) aggregates 18 mixed templates, mostly persona/narrative/format framings. It cannot show a compliant-prefix or suffix effect, and it serves as a contrast to GAS@18, not as a test of V4.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Sections 4–5 use jailbreak attacks and shallow-alignment findings to motivate and evaluate BCA/GAS; aggregate attack results do not establish the specific bypass mechanisms in V4.

tranche.reason: Uses jailbreak transformations and adaptive attacks to evaluate bounded harmful reachability and search performance. It does not isolate compliant-prefix or suffix effects, compare aligned-versus-base token distributions, or test another listed claim version.

source_check.notes: Table 1 and §4.2.1 confirm the quoted direct-prompt results for instruction-tuned checkpoints. BCA preserves original probabilities on retained branches; its bounded harmful mass excludes discarded branches and depends on the harm evaluator.
